title: Table with PPT at OpenStreetsPGH!
description:
Pittsburghers for Public Transit Needs YOUR Help at OpenStreetsPGH! 

Join Pittsburghers for Public Transit (PPT) at OpenStreetsPGH (https://openstreetspgh.org/) to learn about the ongoing transit funding crisis, its potential impact on riders in the City of Pittsburgh, and how you can join other riders around the county to say no to service cuts, fare hikes, and route eliminations. 

Members tabling with PPT can expect to sit and hangout at the PPT tent, greet passers by and folks who approach our table, give an introduction of PPT and engage them around their transit experiences. The environment is casual and fun.

What Will We Do?

Your voice is crucial in advocating for robust public transit funding. At our table, we will be;

Share opportunities to contact your elected officials and share your concerns.

Talk to attendees about how to get involved with Pittsburghers for Public Transit and our efforts to fight for equitable and accessible transit.

Collect stories from fellow riders about the importance of public transit in their lives.

We will have a young riders’ craft corner, where little ones can make and decorate their own bus pass lanyard!

Pittsburghers for Public Transit is a grassroots union of transit riders, workers and neighbors. Together we organize for an expanded, affordable and accessible public transit system that meets all needs, with no communities left behind.

title: North Idaho Town Hall Phone Bank (8/26)
description:
Please join us for a virtual phone bank ahead of our North Idaho town halls! On August 26th, we’ll be meeting at 5:30pm MT via Zoom to make phone calls to community members to invite them to upcoming town halls.

During the 2025 legislative session, Idaho lawmakers passed House Bill 93 and enacted a $50 million school-voucher program. For the first time in state history, Idaho tax dollars will be used to subsidize the cost of tuition for private-school families.

The special-interest groups promoting vouchers have made clear that the $50 million program is only the beginning. During next year’s legislative session, they intend to remove the $50-million cap and expand the program to all private-school families, including the wealthy, at an estimated cost of $339 million per year.

Such a massive expansion of vouchers would bankrupt Idaho and drain millions from public schools. For the benefit of a small number of private-school families, it would defund the public education system that serves 94% of Idaho’s kids.

It may be inevitable that the legislature tries to expand House Bill 93, but it is not inevitable that they will succeed. To stop this attack on public schools, we need to get organized. Please sign up if you can make it and we hope to see you soon!

Please join us for a virtual phone bank ahead of our North Idaho town halls! On September 16th, we’ll be meeting at 5:30pm MT via Zoom to make phone calls to community members to invite them to upcoming town halls.

During the 2025 legislative session, Idaho lawmakers passed House Bill 93 and enacted a $50 million school-voucher program. For the first time in state history, Idaho tax dollars will be used to subsidize the cost of tuition for private-school families.

The special-interest groups promoting vouchers have made clear that the $50 million program is only the beginning. During next year’s legislative session, they intend to remove the $50-million cap and expand the program to all private-school families, including the wealthy, at an estimated cost of $339 million per year.

Such a massive expansion of vouchers would bankrupt Idaho and drain millions from public schools. For the benefit of a small number of private-school families, it would defund the public education system that serves 94% of Idaho’s kids.

It may be inevitable that the legislature tries to expand House Bill 93, but it is not inevitable that they will succeed. To stop this attack on public schools, we need to get organized. Please sign up if you can make it and we hope to see you soon!

title: Broken Vows Town Hall: Families vs. the Big Ugly Bill
description:
**Broken Vows Town Hall: Families vs. the Big Ugly Bill**  
*Vows to Billionaires, Cuts to Us*

Congressman Bresnahan is getting married before the year is out—but he’s already **broken his promises** to the people of this district.

By voting for the Big Ugly Bill, he turned his back on working families—slashing **Medicaid** and **SNAP**, undermining **affordable housing**, attacking **immigrant communities**, and putting the **stability of our local hospitals** at risk—all while giving away **tax breaks to billionaires** and corporations. From Scranton to every corner of the district, families are feeling the impact.

That’s why we’re gathering at the **Greenridge Club**—a venue known for hosting weddings, now hosting a very different kind of event.

Fair Share America, Pennsylvanians Together, Pennsylvanians Policy Center, Planned Parenthood PA, Action Together NEPA, Commonwealth Communications, For Our Future, MomsRising, and our local partners are hosting this town hall because the system is rigged—and it’s time we start fighting back.Join us for a **district-wide town hall** where residents, advocates, and community leaders will:

- Expose the harm caused by the Big Ugly Bill  
- Hold Congressman Bresnahan accountable  
- Demand an economy—and a democracy—that puts **families first**
